narrative:
The model predicted a 64% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability exceeded the school's acceptance threshold, your law school application was denied.

The decision was driven primarily by three aspects of your academic record. Your third-year class ranking had the strongest influence and worked in your favor: placing in the 9th decile is noticeably stronger than the average 5.8 decile among accepted students, which pulled the prediction toward passing. However, two other factors pushed harder in the opposite direction. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.0 sits below the 3.23 average of accepted applicants and was the second-most important reason the model leaned toward failure. Your first-year class ranking in the 6th decile, while average for accepted students, still added a smaller but meaningful push toward predicting you would struggle with the bar exam.

Taken together, these academic signals outweighed the positive effect of your stronger third-year performance and your upper-middle family income, which the model treated as fairly typical.

You should focus on strengthening the areas the model flagged. Retaking courses to raise your undergraduate GPA, seeking additional bar-prep support, or gaining practical legal experience could improve your profile for future applications. Consider reapplying once you have demonstrated clearer evidence of readiness for the bar.
